- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged downward trends; model shows mean reversion too slowly or not at all.
- Forecast tends to be too high in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after a recent peak; adjust downward by 5–10% for the first 5–7 days.
- Model often fails to capture the “rebound” after a sharp drop — underestimates recovery phase.
- When history shows strong volatility, model over-smooths; introduce a volatility multiplier or adaptive filter to respond to high variance.
- Forecast tends to be too optimistic in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day window — reduce by 3–5% for the last 7 days if recent price is trending down.
- If the last 5 days show a clear downward trend, model often fails to recognize it — apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% for the next 5 days.
- Model frequently overestimates the “mean” of the 30-day window — adjust by subtracting 1–3% of the average historical deviation from the mean.
